hackerone_ineligible_criteria_reference.source: HackerOne Core Policy - Major Ineligible Findings

critical_exclusions.clause: Clickjacking on pages without sensitive actions
critical_exclusions.implication: Must demonstrate actual state-changing operations (e.g., account takeover, unauthorized transfer) to be eligible.

critical_exclusions.clause: Missing CSP headers, SSL/TLS flaws, missing HttpOnly flags
critical_exclusions.implication: Informational/N/A unless directly chained with a high-impact vulnerability.

critical_exclusions.clause: Self-XSS, theoretical race conditions, software version disclosure
critical_exclusions.implication: Automatically closed as N/A without a functional PoC achieving 200 OK or state change.

hackerone_ineligible_criteria_reference.actionable_takeaway: Focus strictly on business logic bypasses (BOLA/IDOR/Mass Assignment) and high-impact UI Redress with clear impact proofs.

next_logic_strategy.action: Pivot from purely visual UI redress to state-changing API parameter manipulation with 200 OK responses.

focus_vectors: TON Space Recovery Email Parameter Tampering

stream_calculation_config.purpose: Safe trace calculation of inputs and state transitions without payload execution

metrics_engine_config.focus: Real-time stream metrics & statistical latency analysis (P95/P99)

zeroday_course_definition.concept: Lucifuge-Style High Density Payload & Time Gap Capture
zeroday_course_definition.definition: Structuring transient execution delays and overstuffed parameters that mimic valid 'PASS' responses into a verifiable zero-day attack vector.
zeroday_course_definition.bounty_reporting_strategy: Present raw calculations, standard-compliant logs, and tree-branching evidence to prove logic failure prior to patch.
